messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: P0 — gpu-node-34 (us-east-1a) kernel panic / kubelet NotReady. Impact: several model endpoints showing 503s and elevated latency :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Triggered pager on team 'oncall' — escalation policy active.

Alex (oncall): acked — taking incident. I'm on call, pinging SRE and Infra.

Jamie (SRE): on it. seeing abrupt node drop from cluster metrics, kubelet lost heartbeat ~2m ago.

Lee (Infra): noted. any nvme/errors in logs? could be host-level hw panic.

Alex (oncall): customer-facing impact: ~8% of requests to /generate are returning 503s; affected model group = r-inference/gpu-large-prod in us-east-1a.

Sam (Customer Success): flagging high usage customers (acct: matchai, acct: fintechly) — they have active pipelines. I'll prep comms once we know ETA.

Jamie (SRE): I'm running initial checks. pulling node logs and system journal.

ops-bot: running playbook -> /runbooks/gpu-node-kernel-panic.md (link)").replace("/runbooks/gpu-node-kernel-panic.md","/runbooks/gpu-node-kernel-panic.md") + "

Jamie (SRE): logs show kernel: 'kernel panic - not syncing: BUG' and NVRM errors; nvme SMART errors prior to panic. snippet:```text
kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, Channel exception
kernel: nvme 1: nvme_cmd_status: error - status 0x4
kernel: kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt
```

Alex (oncall): ok, plan: cordon + drain node to remove from scheduler, route traffic to spare pool, then attempt graceful reboot and serial-console capture. If node unresponsive, isolate and escalate to hardware vendor.

Jamie (SRE): running commands now:
```bash
kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu-node-34
kubectl cordon gpu-node-34
kubectl drain gpu-node-34 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

Lee (Infra): I'll attach to serial console and attempt to capture kernel oops and dmesg. prepping ipmi/console. If it's nvme, we should avoid repeated reboots until we confirm disk state.

ops-bot: autoscaling policy triggered — creating temporary extra capacity in us-east-1 to absorb disrupted pods (adding 2 nodes to 'gpu-spare-pool').

Alex (oncall): routing update: traffic shifted 70% to gpu-spare-pool, 30% remains straggling — monitoring errors.

Sam (Customer Success): sending an interim note to affected customers: "We're investigating degraded model performance in us-east-1; teams are mitigating; we'll post updates in 15 mins."

Jamie (SRE): drain completed for 86 pods, 4 pods failed to terminate (stateful/local-data). For the failed pods I'm triggering restart on alternative nodes.

Alex (oncall): starting node reboot via IPMI now (soft reboot).

Lee (Infra): serial console shows repeated nvme errors and kernel oops on POST. collecting crashdump (kdump) and taking NVMe SMART logs.

Jamie (SRE): any 503s now? error rate down to ~1.2% from 8% — good. latency back to normal for most calls.

Alex (oncall): paging update to PD: acknowledged and mitigated to partial failure — continuing investigation and hardware RMA prep.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by Alex (oncall) — escalation paused.

Lee (Infra): filing vendor ticket: RMA request + attaching logs and crashdump. Ticket #HW-11223. ETA for replacement: 48-72h unless overnight ship.

Jamie (SRE): we've pinned a short-term routing fallback in the control plane: any route requests for r-inference/gpu-large-prod in us-east-1a will now prefer replicas in us-east-1b and dedicated-pool nodes. This should eliminate customer-visible errors while node is repaired.

Sam (Customer Success): updating customers with ETA and mitigation steps. leaving note to escalate if they see any regression.

Alex (oncall): handing off to Lee (Infra) for hardware follow-up and RMA. I'll keep monitoring and will re-open if we see regression. moving to post-incident doc.

Lee (Infra): taking ownership for HW work and RMA; will update ticket and close when replacement validated.

Jamie (SRE): post-incident action items: 1) add stronger nvme pre-fail alerts; 2) verify kdump collection in prod images; 3) add more graceful drain retries for stateful pods. I'll create GH issues.

Alex (oncall): thanks team. incident closed to oncall — moving to postmortem -> link to doc will be posted in channel.

ops-bot: incident summary: Impact partially mitigated; routing fallback applied; node isolated; RMA opened; customer notifications sent.

Sam (Customer Success): will follow up with customers once RMA confirmed.

(End of thread)
